footer: Ember Arena — built in the browser with three.js. No Blender on the server.

versions.title: Bootstrap
versions.summary: The first browser-native arena: eight team portals, a central lava pool, 64 sprite units, a 640×360 pixel-art pass and a HUD shell.
versions.note: Independent review: 35/100. A solid pipeline baseline, but the arena is still a small blockout in a black void. M1 focuses on framing, lighting and the 32×32 octagonal layout.

versions.title: Arena Blockout
versions.summary: Dense 32×32 octagonal arena with eight radial spawn zones, a larger central lava objective, a terrain apron and a cleaner portal prefab.
versions.note: Independent review: 50/100 (M0: 35). The arena now fills the frame, the octagon and eight team gates are in place, and the HUD has a minimap, commander panel and ability grid. Remaining gaps: floor value, lava scale, unit silhouettes and portal energy.

versions.title: Simulation Core
versions.summary: Eight-team combat with waves, spatial-hash targeting, melee, arrows, crits, health bars, death states and a live battlefield HUD.
versions.note: Internal estimate ~54/100. 196 units, 164 kills, 60 draw calls and 144 FPS in the in-app browser. The art pass (M3) and VFX (M4) are next.

versions.title: Terrain Art Pass
versions.summary: Mid-value stone, a 2.5× lava basin, taller cliffs, outlying huts and unified violet portals.
versions.note: Estimated ~61/100. Bloom, damage numbers and elemental bursts landed in the next pass.

versions.title: VFX and Feel
versions.summary: Quarter-res bloom, lightning/fire/poison spells, death bursts, outlined damage text and arrow trails.
versions.note: Estimated ~64/100. 280 units at 144 FPS and 72 draw calls. HUD/minimap polish is next.

versions.title: HUD and Minimap
versions.summary: Clickable team selection, a real minimap, original SVG ability art, command grid and four central violet barriers.
versions.note: Independent review: 61/100. The minimap, altar, bloom and HUD improved, but terrain material and unit identity still hold the gate. Estimated 71-74 after the six prioritized fixes.

versions.title: Pixel-Tilemap Reboot
versions.summary: The battlefield is now a 2D 2:1 pixel-art tilemap: a 64×64 pannable map, baked flagstone and Voronoi lava, eight bases, four-direction unit sprites, authored spell sheets and a canvas pixel HUD.
versions.note: Independent review: 57/100 (M5: 61 — different medium). The pixel pivot fixed projection, 1:1 sampling, the map and the HUD; the remaining gap is art density, unit silhouettes, VFX scale and the empty plaza centre. 5 draw calls, 83 FPS at 224 units.

versions.title: Portal, Altar and Sprite Pass
versions.summary: Framed stone portals with a white-hot core now anchor the bases, a three-tier brazier-lit altar carries a faceted red crystal, and a broken-wall ruin plus mid-field ruins fill the plaza. Lava was re-keyed to dark basalt plates under broken white-hot seams, the floor ramp darkened, units rebuilt at 48×64 with 3-tone armour and team-banded shields, and the HUD skinned with an armoured portrait and a filled inventory.
versions.note: Independent review: 62/100 (M6: 57). Terrain and HUD moved; VFX is still 48, and the ice nova remains a translucent overlay that erases the units beneath it — that is the binding gap for M8.

versions.title: Gate Attempt 1: Basalt, Nova and Brass
versions.summary: Multi-scale dark basalt lava plates now sit under hot seams, the ice nova is rebuilt as an opaque, dark-outlined 14-shard burst over a scorch pool with stepped frost rings, and the fire is authored four-tone pixel art that casts light onto the ground. Team colour moved off the 2 px sash onto the cloth torso, and a wide bow silhouette makes the archer readable at 1×. The HUD gained a 5-step brass bezel, carved bronze panels, a 2× portrait, 2× icons and framed inventory slots, and a new headless `make probe` tool reports FPS, draw calls and console errors without a browser window.
versions.note: Independent review: 67/100 (M7: 62). Layout 62, Terrain 63, Units 66, VFX 63, HUD 82, Pixel art 66. HUD is the first category above 80; the gate needs 90 with no category below 80. The committed capture also absorbs the review's lava value inversion, cast light and connected nova shards, which are not re-scored.

gallery.caption: 2× detail of the altar at cam=30,30: opaque shard nova, four-tone flame and pink, teal and olive cloth torsos on the surrounding units.
Exact capture the independent 67/100 review measured; the committed m8.png is the same URL with the post-review fixes.

versions.title: Rust-Ready Reference
versions.summary: Frozen schemas, asset manifest, deterministic traces and a port plan for a Rust/WASM core.
versions.note: Planned. No Rust or networking work starts before the visual gate is signed off.

versions.title: Footmen Frenzy Match Loop
versions.summary: Units now spawn from their own barracks, team 0 selects and attack-moves them to the middle, the plaza portals are gone, and a wall ring with one gate per courtyard forces every base-to-base route through the altar. A shared map-geometry source drives both the simulation collision and the pixel tilemap; stone causeways cross the four cardinal lava pools. Every team starts with archers, buys a 150-gold swordsman upgrade, and researches a 200-gold Frenzy charge; the AI runs the same loop so the capture stays dense.
versions.note: Independent review: 72/100 (M9: 72), weighted 72.25. Layout 71, Terrain 70, Units 71, VFX 66, HUD 83, Pixel art 69. The loop's core claim is proven: no portals, one dense plaza scrum, readable gate/causeway enclosure in the west detail, and a HUD reporting gold, tier, supply and upgrade/Frenzy costs. What still binds: thinned wings/upper field, flat screen-aligned wall bricks, VFX 66. Captures are at t=25; 331 units, 5 draw calls, 60.0 FPS, console clean.

gallery.caption: West courtyard at cam=14,32: the Ember barracks door, the wall ring and gate, and a stone causeway cutting the cardinal lava pool.
2x altar detail at cam=31,31: archers and swordsmen in the central scrum, damage numerals, health bars and the nova.

versions.title: Framing, Molten Cores and the Gate
versions.summary: The scored frame now encloses the fight: an interior rampart with a ruined arch and gate sits behind the melee, so the battle reads in front of architecture rather than on an open field. Every lava field carries one offset molten core with dark crust islands, white-hot cracks and three directional flow seams, over a cooler grey floor and wider basalt plates. The west, east and north lanes gained authored ruin, conifer, crystal and brazier clumps, while the barracks-spawn, attack-move and upgrade loop from M10 is unchanged.
versions.note: Independent review: 75.2 weighted (M10: 72.25). Layout 78, Terrain 77, Units 71, VFX 67, HUD 83, Pixel art 69. The gate stays blocked on Units/VFX. Three review rounds: 73.8 → 74.6 → 75.2. Wall plinth absorbed after scoring. The most binding item is VFX: the nova is still a smooth cyan gradient web with hard white alpha-square glows, and the unit melee remains a fused-outline carpet with no front line or attack pose.

gallery.caption: The west courtyard: causeway, wall ring, barracks and the new interior rampart.
2× detail of the NW gate: ruined arch, brazier and crenellated wall run.
2× altar melee, showing the molten lava and swordsman silhouettes.

versions.title: Stepped Nova and Atmosphere
versions.summary: The altar nova is now an opaque, dark-outlined, per-pixel stepped ice star with flat value bands over a dim ground ring, and the frame is closed by a stepped edge vignette while enlarged lava embers sit alongside wing-confined dust and visible brazier, torch and gate cast pools. The altar crystal is rebuilt as a faceted, dark-outlined shard with a visible split, and the clipped alpha-square glow helpers are gone. The M10/M11 match loop, enclosure and lava craft are unchanged.
versions.note: Independent review: 77.1 weighted (M11: 75.2, +1.9). Layout 78, Terrain 77, Units 71, VFX 79, HUD 83, Pixel art 70. VFX clears the task's ≥75 bar (79). Gate still blocked on Units 71 (task 017) and VFX 79; the task's total ≥83 was unreachable from a 15%-weight category. Nova measured 750 → 15 ice colours with 2 px transitions; vignette corner/inset ratio 0.773 with every edge band darker than M11; embers 526 → 714 hot dots; gate cast light +33.9 L; no alpha squares; world 6-bit colours 736 vs M11 737. 331 units, 5 draw calls, 60 FPS, console clean.

gallery.caption: 2× altar detail at cam=31,31: the opaque stepped ice star, faceted crystal and hard value bands.
West courtyard at cam=14,32: lava embers, brazier cast pools, wall/gate craft and the stepped vignette.

versions.title: Readable Ranks and Per-Unit Fill
versions.summary: Every unit is now a single cropped quad with a tight baked contact shadow, cutting the frame from 4,528 to ~2,990 px per unit (−34%) with the feet anchor unchanged. The design cap moved 400 → 256 so the t=25 plaza holds 207 soldiers who read as ranks instead of a carpet, carried by full-face team shields, an attack/guard stance while fighting, and 11×2 green/amber/red health bars on a staggered baseline. Damage numerals stack vertically and cap at 16.
versions.note: Independent review: 78.35 weighted (M12: 77.1, +1.25). Layout 77 (−1), Terrain 77, Units 80 (+9), VFX 79, HUD 83, Pixel art 71. Units clears the 017 bar at exactly the floor, but the gate needs 90 with no category below 80, so Layout, Terrain, VFX and Pixel art still block it; the layout drop is the price of the cap and must be recovered with props, not atmosphere. Measured 60.0 FPS at the capture (221 units, 1,110 quads) and at t=92 (242 units, 1,014 quads), 5 draw calls, console clean, golden hash unchanged at 3198708409.

West courtyard at cam=14,32: sparse ranks and lit floor between neighbours after the 400 → 256 cap, with the wall ring, causeway and lava field unchanged.
